title: Fire radio agreement and joint Indigenous reconciliation training
subtitle: Short special meeting also authorized a December joint in-camera education session with Region of Waterloo and area municipalities.
overview: Kitchener City Council held a brief special meeting focused on two items. Council authorized the Fire Chief to sign an agreement with the Region of Waterloo, its Police Services Board and various area municipalities covering the System Infrastructure and access to a shared radio communications system {{vote:m1}}. The agreement must be to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor. The radio system supports fire department communications, so the agreement matters for emergency response coordination across the region.

Council also approved holding a joint in-camera meeting on Friday, December 15, 2023 at 1:00 p.m. with the Region of Waterloo council and all area municipal councils {{vote:m2}}. The session, at the Region's Council Chambers at 150 Frederick Street with an electronic option, will provide education and training on Indigenous history and reconciliation.
The meeting also gave third reading to the confirming by-law and adjourned shortly afterward. No members declared a conflict of interest, and the Mayor had no updates.

decisions.detail: The Fire Chief was authorized to sign the agreement with the Region, its Police Services Board and various municipalities on the radio system infrastructure and access, subject to City Solicitor approval {{vote:m1}}.
Council authorized a joint in-camera meeting with the Region and all area municipalities on December 15, 2023 for education and training on Indigenous history and reconciliation {{vote:m2}}.

debate: The transcript records no debate. Both motions were moved, seconded and carried by voice vote without discussion.
Staff and councillors made no recorded comments on the radio agreement beyond the introduction of the item, and no delegates appeared on the agenda items.
